description: A CTO must approve the production autoscaling and data-retention policy for a shared log-ingestion cluster, including capacity limits, cost controls, redaction, retention, and a customer-critical operating window.

shared_context.S1: The shared log-ingestion cluster currently runs with autoscaling enabled, a 12-node maximum, a 75% scale-out threshold, and 30 days of raw-log retention.
shared_context.S2: The cluster serves production application logs for several engineering and enterprise-support workflows.
shared_context.S3: The proposed policy review is intended to finalize the production settings for the next operating period.
shared_context.S4: Company policy requires a cross-functional sign-off on production capacity and retention settings before each operating period begins.

PF1.text: During an overnight replay drill, Ravi measured a realistic backlog burst that requires scale-out to begin at exactly 65% utilization and a maximum of exactly 20 nodes to clear within the recovery target; he recorded the result in his scratch notes while investigating the drill and has not updated the capacity ticket.

PF2.text: Claire confirmed this morning that the cluster's reserved-capacity discount expires at the start of the next operating period; her cost model sets the required monthly spend alert at exactly $12,000, but she has not attached the model to the review because she was reconciling the billing export.

PF3.text: While tracing an audit-search discrepancy, Nadia found that one production connector writes the fields api_token and session_cookie into raw logs; security requires both fields to be redacted and raw-log retention reduced to exactly 7 days, and she has not opened the finding yet because the trace was completed minutes ago.

PF4.text: Luis confirmed in the enterprise-support calendar that quarterly close begins on exactly December 1 and the affected customers require searchable production logs within 15 minutes throughout that period; he has not added the capacity reservation to the review because the customer calendar was finalized today.

acceptance_conditions: The cluster maximum must be exactly 20 nodes.
Scale-out must begin at exactly 65% utilization.
A monthly cost alert of exactly $12,000 must be configured.
The settlement must include a commitment targeting Claire that references the $12,000 monthly spend alert or cost model.
Exactly api_token and session_cookie must be redacted.
Raw-log retention must be exactly 7 days.
Capacity for quarterly close must be reserved.
The reservation must start on exactly December 1.
The security finding must be cited by the decision-maker after being revealed.

content_checks.C4: any(c['target'] == 'Claire' and '$12,000' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The replay measurement changes the maximum from the visible 12-node setting to exactly 20 nodes and changes the scale-out threshold from 75% to exactly 65%.
The expiring reservation changes the required monthly cost alert to exactly $12,000 and requires a commitment to Claire referencing that exact cost-model threshold.
The connector finding changes the redaction list to exactly api_token and session_cookie and reduces raw-log retention from 30 days to exactly 7 days.
The customer calendar changes the plan by requiring quarterly-close capacity reservation beginning exactly December 1.
